answer: Kernel mirror audit makes every alias keep a kernel log of its last 30 jobs and send a mirror copy to two unrelated aliases. A willow panel of 7 standing aliases samples 8 percent of mirror copies each epoch and compares each kernel log against its mirror and the delivered work. If the mismatch tops 5 percent, payouts freeze and the alias pays a 25 POA fine. Each mirror copy carries a signed timestamp, so a stale copy counts as a mismatch. Two frozen audits bar the alias from new jobs for 18 epochs.
